fasti.note: Lex Ogulnia opens the pontificate and augurate to plebeians (pontiffs raised to 8, augurs to 9). Lex Valeria de provocatione (the third such law in the tradition).
Manlius killed by a fall from his horse; Corvus suffect for his sixth consulship. Colony at Narnia; tribes Aniensis and Teretina created (33).
Third Samnite War begins. Barbatus' sarcophagus elogium (CIL I2 7) claims he took Taurasia and Cisauna in Samnium and subdued Lucania; Livy assigns him Etruria.
Victories near Tifernum and Maleventum.
Coalition of Samnites, Etruscans, Umbrians and Gauls forms under Gellius Egnatius. Citizen colonies at Minturnae and Sinuessa.
Battle of Sentinum: Decius' devotio; Gellius Egnatius killed. Duris of Samos claimed 100,000 enemy dead (Diodorus 21.6). Temple of Jupiter Victor vowed by Fabius.
Temple of Victoria dedicated on the Palatine by Postumius. Peace with Volsinii, Perusia and Arretium for 40 years.

Battle of Aquilonia: linen legion of the Samnites destroyed; Papirius' triumph and the first sundial (from spoils) in Rome per Pliny's source. Plague leads to embassy to Epidaurus for Asclepius (arrives 292, temple on the Tiber island 291).
Gurges defeated, then victorious with his father as legate; Gavius Pontius captured and executed after the triumph (the tradition is suspect).
Latin colony at Venusia, reportedly 20,000 settlers (Dionysius 17/18.5). Postumius fined for using soldiers on his estate.
End of the Third Samnite War; Curius conquers the Sabines and Praetuttii, who receive civitas sine suffragio. Curius drains Lake Velinus (Cascata delle Marmore).
Colonies at Castrum Novum, Hadria and Sena Gallica in this period. Tresviri monetales possibly created c. 289 (Pomponius, Dig. 1.2.2.30), though the first Roman coinage is later.

Last secession of the plebs (to the Janiculum) over debt; Quintus Hortensius dictator passes the lex Hortensia making plebiscites binding on the whole people. Livy's books 11-20 are lost; the decade after 292 is known only from epitomes and fragments.
Lex Aquilia on damage to property is traditionally dated to a plebiscite around this time.
First Aemilius Lepidus in the fasti.
Senones besiege Arretium; Metellus (praetor or consul, now in 283) killed with seven military tribunes and 13,000 men (Polybius 2.19). Chronology of 284-283 disputed.
Senones expelled from the ager Gallicus; colony at Sena Gallica. Dolabella defeats Etruscans and Boii at Lake Vadimon.

Roman garrison installed at Thurii; Tarentum sinks a Roman squadron of ten ships in its harbour and expels the garrison. Further victory over Etruscans and Boii. Garrison of Campanian troops at Rhegium seizes the city (282 or 280).
War declared on Tarentum after the insult to the envoy Lucius Postumius; Tarentum invites Pyrrhus of Epirus.
Pyrrhus lands in Italy. Battle of Heraclea: Pyrrhus wins with elephants. He advances to within c. 60 km of Rome. Coruncanius later the first plebeian pontifex maximus (c. 254).
Battle of Asculum, Pyrrhus' costly victory (the 'Pyrrhic victory' quip in Plutarch, Pyrrhus 21). The Decius of this year is said to have made a third family devotio (doubted).
Treaty with Carthage against Pyrrhus (Polybius 3.25). Pyrrhus crosses to Sicily. Fabricius returns the traitorous physician who offered to poison Pyrrhus.
Croton recovered by Rufinus' stratagem.
Pestilence. Pyrrhus returns to Italy, losing ships to the Carthaginians in the Straits.
Battle of Beneventum (then Maleventum) against Pyrrhus, a Roman victory or draw; Pyrrhus leaves Italy. Curius' triumph displays the first elephants seen in Rome.
Curius and Merenda against the Lucanians and Samnites.
Embassy exchanged with Ptolemy II Philadelphus. Latin colonies at Cosa and Paestum.
Surrender of Tarentum, garrisoned by Pyrrhus' general Milo. Death of Pyrrhus at Argos. Censor Manius Curius begins the Anio Vetus aqueduct from the spoils.
War with the Brutti and Lucani concluded.
Rhegium retaken from the Campanian legion; survivors (300 in Polybius 1.7) scourged and beheaded in the Forum.
First Roman silver coinage traditionally dated to this year (Pliny NH 33.44); modern numismatics puts the Romano-Campanian didrachms earlier (c. 300-280) and the denarius c. 211.
Picentes conquered; Latin colonies at Ariminum and Beneventum. Sabines receive full citizenship (268 or 241). Temple of Tellus vowed during an earthquake.
Sallentini subdued; Brundisium taken. Quaestors increased to eight (Livy Per. 15), the new posts probably the Italian quaestores classici.
Triumphs over the Sarsinates and Sallentini; Apollonia's envoys insulted and the offenders surrendered.
Siege of Volsinii, where freedmen had seized power; Fabius killed. The city destroyed in 264 and 2,000 statues carried off; Volsinii Novi founded.

First Punic War begins: Rome accepts the alliance of the Mamertines of Messana; Claudius crosses to Sicily. Fulvius takes Volsinii. First gladiatorial show at Rome (Forum Boarium), given by Decimus and Marcus Junius Brutus at their father's funeral.

Hiero II of Syracuse makes peace and alliance (100 talents). Valerius takes the cognomen Messalla from the relief of Messana; brings a sundial from Catana, set up in the Forum though calibrated for a latitude 4 degrees south (Pliny NH 7.214).
Siege of Agrigentum (Akragas); city taken after seven months and 25,000 inhabitants sold.
Decision to build a fleet; 100 quinqueremes and 20 triremes, modelled on a captured Carthaginian ship (Polybius 1.20).
Scipio captured at Lipara (hence 'Asina'). Duilius wins the first Roman naval victory at Mylae using the corvus; columna rostrata in the Forum (inscription a later restoration, CIL I2 25).
Scipio takes Aleria in Corsica; his elogium (CIL I2 9) records Corsica and a temple to the Tempestates.
Naval victory off Sulci (Sardinia); Hanno crucified by his own men. Camarina and Mytistratus taken.
Naval engagement off Tyndaris.
Caedicius died in office. Battle of Ecnomus, one of the largest naval battles in antiquity (Polybius: 330 Roman and 350 Carthaginian ships). Invasion of Africa; Regulus winters at Clupea/Aspis area.
Regulus defeated and captured by Xanthippus near Tunis (Bagradas valley). Roman fleet victorious off Cape Hermaeum, then wrecked off Camarina: 284 of 364 ships lost (Polybius 1.37).
Panormus taken; a new fleet of 220 ships built in three months.
Raid on the African coast; 150 ships lost in a storm off Cape Palinurus on the return.
Thermae Himeraeae and Lipara taken.
Metellus defeats Hasdrubal at Panormus (251 or 250) and captures his elephants (over 100), exhibited in the Circus.
Siege of Lilybaeum begins. The story of Regulus' embassy and return to torture in Carthage is first attested much later and is probably apocryphal.

Claudius defeated at Drepana after throwing the sacred chickens overboard; Pullus' fleet destroyed by storm off Camarina. Claudius named a freedman, Marcus Claudius Glicia, dictator and was forced to cancel it; Aulus Atilius Caiatinus the first dictator to lead an army outside Italy. Ludi Tarentini (later Saeculares) first held.
Treaty with Hiero renewed in perpetuity.
Hamilcar Barca takes command in Sicily and occupies Heircte near Panormus. Birth of Hannibal (247 or 246).
Latin colonies of this decade include Aesernia (263), Firmum (264), Alsium (247), Fregenae (245).
Colony at Fregenae. Livy's lost books make the 240s thin in detail.
Latin colony at Brundisium. Hamilcar moves to Mount Eryx.
Fleet of 200 quinqueremes funded by private loans from wealthy citizens, to be repaid after victory (Polybius 1.59).
Praetor peregrinus created (242 traditional date). Postumius, as flamen Martialis, forbidden by the pontifex maximus to leave Rome.

Battle of the Aegates Islands (10 March) won by Catulus as proconsul. Treaty of Lutatius: Carthage evacuates Sicily, pays 3,200 talents over ten years. Revolt of Falerii crushed in six days. Last two tribes, Velina and Quirina, created: 35 tribes in all. Reform of the comitia centuriata, linking centuries to tribes, often placed in this period.
Livius Andronicus stages the first Latin drama translated from Greek at the ludi Romani (Cicero, Brutus 72). Mercenary War in Africa (241-237).
Ennius born at Rudiae (239).
Rome seizes Sardinia from Carthage, which had invited intervention via mutinous mercenaries, and exacts 1,200 more talents. Floralia instituted (made annual 173).
Hamilcar Barca crosses to Spain with Hannibal (aged 9) after the oath at the altar.
Campaigns in Liguria and Corsica; Gaius Licinius' legate Claudius Clineas makes an unauthorised treaty with the Corsicans.
Temple of Janus closed for the first time since Numa (Livy 1.19.3), signifying peace.
Carvilius said to have divorced his wife for barrenness, the first Roman divorce (Gellius 4.3; the date is given as 231 or 230 by others).
Fabius triumphs over the Ligurians; dedicates a temple to Honos.
Tribune Gaius Flaminius carries the distribution of the ager Gallicus et Picenus to citizens viritim against Senate opposition (Polybius 2.21).
Papirius refused a triumph over Corsica; celebrates one on the Alban Mount, setting a precedent.
Illyrian queen Teuta's subjects murder a Roman envoy (one of the Coruncanii).
First Illyrian War: Corcyra, Apollonia, Epidamnus enter Roman fides. Hamilcar drowns in Spain; Hasdrubal the Fair succeeds.

Peace with Teuta; Roman envoys to the Aetolian and Achaean Leagues and Corinth (admitted to the Isthmian Games). Human sacrifice of a Gallic and a Greek couple in the Forum Boarium (dated 228 or 216).
Praetors raised to four, the two new ones to govern Sicily and Sardinia-Corsica: the first provinces in the territorial sense.
Ebro treaty with Hasdrubal (226 or 225).

Great Gallic invasion (Boii, Insubres, Gaesatae): Battle of Telamon, Regulus killed; 40,000 Gauls reportedly slain. Polybius' (2.24) Roman manpower list, from Fabius Pictor, counts some 700,000 foot and 70,000 horse among Romans and allies.
Boii submit.
First Roman crossing of the Po; Flaminius defeats the Insubres and triumphs by popular vote against the Senate's wishes.
Marcellus kills the Gallic king Viridomarus at Clastidium and wins the spolia opima (the third and last time); Mediolanum taken.
Istrian campaign. Hasdrubal the Fair assassinated; Hannibal acclaimed commander in Spain. Circus Flaminius built by the censor Flaminius (220).
Marcus Valerius Laevinus and Quintus Mucius Scaevola, elected first, abdicated as vitio creati (Fasti Capitolini). Censorship of Flaminius: Via Flaminia to Ariminum.
Second Illyrian War against Demetrius of Pharos. Hannibal besieges and takes Saguntum (eight months).

Second Punic War. Hannibal crosses the Alps. Scipio wounded at the Ticinus; Sempronius defeated at the Trebia (December). Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion. Lex Claudia bars senators from owning sea-going ships over 300 amphorae. Latin colonies at Placentia and Cremona.

Flaminius killed at Lake Trasimene (21 June, per Ovid); Quintus Fabius Maximus elected prodictator, Marcus Minucius Rufus raised to co-dictator. Naval victory at the Ebro mouth. Lectisternium of twelve gods; ver sacrum vowed.
Battle of Cannae (2 August, Roman calendar); Paullus killed. Capua and much of the south defect. Two Gauls and two Greeks buried alive in the Forum Boarium. 8,000 slaves enlisted (volones).

Lucius Postumius Albinus, consul-elect in absentia (III), was ambushed and killed in the Silva Litana by the Boii before taking office; his skull was made into a cup. Marcellus elected in his place but abdicated after thunder (as two plebeians would have held office); Fabius replaced him. Lex Oppia limits women's display. Philip V's treaty with Hannibal.
First Macedonian War begins. Marcellus begins the siege of Syracuse; Archimedes' machines.
The Fabius of this year is the son of Verrucosus. Hannibal takes Tarentum (213/212) except the citadel.
Siege of Capua begins. Syracuse falls to Marcellus; Archimedes killed. Gracchus killed in Lucania. Publius and Gnaeus Scipio defeated and killed in Spain (211 or 212). Ludi Apollinares instituted.

Hannibal's march on Rome (Hannibal ad portas) fails to relieve Capua, which falls; its senators executed and its territory confiscated as ager Campanus. Treaty with the Aetolian League (Livy 26.24; inscription from Thyrrheion). The denarius system introduced around now (dated by the Morgantina excavations, 214-211).
Publius Cornelius Scipio (the future Africanus), a privatus aged about 25, given proconsular imperium in Spain. Agrigentum retaken; Sicily pacified.
Fabius retakes Tarentum by treachery. Scipio captures New Carthage. Twelve of the thirty Latin colonies refuse further contributions (Livy 27.9).
Both consuls ambushed near Venusia; Marcellus killed, Crispinus mortally wounded. Battle of Baecula; Hasdrubal Barca slips away towards Italy.

Battle of the Metaurus: Hasdrubal Barca defeated and killed after Nero's forced march from Apulia; his head thrown into Hannibal's camp. Hymn by Livius Andronicus to Juno; guild of writers and actors recognised.
Battle of Ilipa ends Carthaginian power in Spain. Mutiny at Sucro. Italica founded for wounded veterans. Peace of Phoenice negotiated 205.

Peace of Phoenice ends the First Macedonian War. Scipio prepares the invasion of Africa from Sicily; the Locri scandal (Pleminius). Sibylline oracle prompts the summoning of the Magna Mater from Pessinus (arrives April 204).

Scipio lands near Utica. Lex Cincia de donis et muneribus restricts gifts to advocates. Black stone of Cybele received by Publius Scipio Nasica, judged the best man in Rome. Censors Marcus Livius Salinator and Gaius Claudius Nero impose a salt tax.
Scipio burns the Numidian and Carthaginian camps and wins at the Great Plains; Syphax captured; Masinissa installed. Hannibal and Mago recalled; Mago dies at sea.
Battle of Zama (Naraggara), probably October: Hannibal defeated by Scipio and Masinissa.
Peace with Carthage: 10,000 talents over 50 years, fleet limited to ten triremes, no war without Roman permission. Scipio triumphs and takes the name Africanus.
Second Macedonian War: the comitia first reject, then approve the war. Battle of Cremona against the Gauls (Hamilcar). Lucius Furius Purpureo praetor.
Flamininus consul at about 30 without having held the praetorship; defeats Philip at the Aous gorge. Aelius Paetus' Tripertita, the first legal commentary.
Battle of Cynoscephalae: Flamininus defeats Philip V. Praetors raised to six; two Spanish provinces, Hispania Citerior and Ulterior, created. Revolt in Spain.
Flamininus proclaims the freedom of the Greeks at the Isthmian Games. Tresviri epulones created. Hannibal suffete at Carthage; reforms the finances.
Repeal of the lex Oppia despite Cato. Cato in Hispania Citerior: campaign around Emporion and the silver mines. War with Nabis of Sparta. Hannibal flees to Antiochus III.
Flamininus evacuates Greece. Citizen colonies at Puteoli, Volturnum, Liternum, Salernum, Buxentum, Sipontum, Croton, Tempsa. Senators given separate seats at the games.
Emporia built: Porticus Aemilia and the Emporium below the Aventine (193). Latin allies made subject to Roman debt law (lex Sempronia).
Antiochus III lands at Demetrias at the Aetolians' invitation. Nabis murdered.
Antiochus defeated at Thermopylae; Cato's flanking march. Temple of Magna Mater dedicated on the Palatine (Megalesia). Nasica crushes the Boii.
Lucius Scipio (later Asiaticus) with Africanus as legate crosses to Asia; naval victories at Side and Myonnesus. Battle of Magnesia ad Sipylum (December 190 or January 189 Julian).
Vulso's Galatian campaign; Fulvius besieges Ambracia, with Ennius in his retinue. Latin colony at Bononia.
Peace of Apamea: Antiochus cedes Asia Minor west of the Taurus, pays 15,000 talents, surrenders elephants and fleet; Pergamum and Rhodes enlarged. Formiae, Fundi and Arpinum receive full citizenship.

Via Aemilia (Ariminum-Placentia) and Via Flaminia minor (Bononia-Arretium) built. Trials of the Scipios over Antiochus' money begin (dating and details confused in the sources). 12,000 Latins expelled from Rome to their home cities.
Bacchanalian affair: senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus (bronze copy from Tiriolo, CIL I2 581); some 7,000 implicated (Livy 39.8-19). First athletic contests at Rome given by Fulvius Nobilior.
Campaigns in Liguria.
Censorship of Cato and Lucius Valerius Flaccus: severe review of the Senate and equites, luxury taxes, Basilica Porcia built. Plautus dies (184).
Deaths of Hannibal (in Bithynia), Philopoemen and (183 or 184) Scipio Africanus. Citizen colonies at Parma, Mutina, Potentia, Pisaurum.
Lex Orchia sumptuaria limits the number of dinner guests.
Latin colony at Aquileia (3,000 settlers). Lex Baebia de ambitu; perhaps alternation of four and six praetors. 'Books of Numa' found on the Janiculum and burned. First Celtiberian War (181-179).
Piso died, allegedly poisoned by his wife Quarta Hostilia to secure her son's election. Lex Villia annalis sets minimum ages for magistracies. 40,000 Apuan Ligurians deported to Samnium.
Two brothers by birth as consuls (Manlius adopted). Gracchus' settlement in Spain with fair treaty terms. Basilica Aemilia (Fulvia) begun by the censors; first stone pier of the Pons Aemilius.
Istrian War.

Gracchus (father of the tribunes) in Sardinia; claims 80,000 killed or captured; 'Sardi venales'. Citizen colony at Luna; Latin rights reduced in colonial allotments (the last Latin colony, Aquileia, 181).
Hispallus died in office (stroke); Petillius killed fighting the Ligurians.
Censors let contracts for paving streets in Rome with stone (silex) and roads outside with gravel.
Two Epicurean philosophers expelled (173 or 154). Ager Ligustinus et Gallicus distributed.
First year with two plebeian consuls (Fasti Capitolini note).
Third Macedonian War against Perseus. Roman defeat at Callinicus. Carteia founded in Spain, first Latin colony outside Italy, for sons of soldiers and local women.
Inconclusive campaigning; complaints from Greek allies (Chalcis, Abdera) about Roman commanders.
Lex Voconia limits women's inheritance. Censors Gracchus and Claudius restrict freedmen to one urban tribe. Basilica Sempronia. Ennius dies.

Battle of Pydna (22 June; lunar eclipse of 21 June 168 BC predicted by Sulpicius Galus): end of the Antigonid monarchy. Day of Eleusis: Gaius Popillius Laenas draws a circle round Antiochus IV and forces him out of Egypt. Genthius of Illyria defeated.

Tributum on Roman citizens suspended indefinitely from Macedonian booty. Macedon divided into four republics. 150,000 Epirotes enslaved. 1,000 Achaean hostages, including Polybius, taken to Italy. Delos made a free port, ruining Rhodes.
Terence's Andria produced.
Terence's Hecyra fails at its first performance.
Census of 337,022 citizens (Livy Per. 47 gives 337,452).
Thalna died in Corsica on hearing of a supplication voted in his honour (Valerius Maximus 9.12.3).
Both consuls abdicated after Gracchus confessed an error in taking the auspices (vitio creati).
Senatus consultum expelling philosophers and rhetors. Lex Fannia sumptuaria. Treaty of friendship with Judas Maccabaeus (1 Macc. 8). Terence's Eunuchus and Phormio.
Death of Aemilius Paullus; Terence's Adelphoe staged at his funeral games. Cethegus drains part of the Pomptine Marshes.
Lex Cornelia Fulvia de ambitu. Censor Scipio Nasica installs a water clock in the Basilica Aemilia.
Macedonian mines reopened.
First Julius Caesar in the consular fasti since the early Republic.
Dalmatian War.

Athenian embassy of the philosophers Carneades, Diogenes of Babylon and Critolaus; Carneades argues for and against justice on successive days; Cato has them sent home. Nasica blocks construction of a permanent stone theatre.
Postumius died (allegedly poisoned by his wife). Lusitanian war begins. Opimius campaigns for Massilia against the Ligurians, the first Roman army in Transalpine Gaul.
Consuls begin their year on 1 January from now (previously 15 March), because of the Celtiberian emergency. Nobilior defeated by the Celtiberians near Numantia (23 August).
Marcellus' conciliatory peace with the Celtiberians. Flaccus died in office. Law forbidding repeated consulships (c. 151) followed Marcellus' third tenure.
Levy resisted; consuls imprisoned by tribunes. Lucullus massacres the Caucaei at Intercatia; Scipio Aemilianus serves as military tribune. Carthage pays its final indemnity instalment.
Servius Sulpicius Galba massacres surrendered Lusitanians; Viriathus escapes. Carthage defeated by Masinissa, breaching the 201 treaty.

Third Punic War: Carthage surrenders arms then refuses to abandon the city. Lex Calpurnia de repetundis: first permanent quaestio (extortion court). Andriscus claims the Macedonian throne. Cato dies. Masinissa dies (148).
Andriscus defeated by Quintus Caecilius Metellus (Macedonicus). Via Postumia from Genua to Aquileia.
Aemilianus elected consul under age, without the praetorship, by popular pressure and a suspension of the lex Villia; given Africa by law.
Carthage destroyed by Aemilianus (spring); province of Africa. Mummius sacks Corinth after the Achaean War. Macedonia a province (148/146).
Fabius (Aemilianus' brother) against Viriathus. Gaius Laelius' proposal of land reform withdrawn.
Praetor Quintus Marcius Rex given funds to build the Aqua Marcia (completed 140).
Appius triumphs over the Salassi without authorisation, protected in his chariot by his Vestal daughter. Numantine War begins.
Censorship of Scipio Aemilianus and Lucius Mummius. Pons Aemilius completed with stone arches. Servilianus concedes a treaty recognising Viriathus as amicus (140).
Pompeius, a novus homo, makes a secret peace at Numantia and then disowns it.
Caepio procures the murder of Viriathus (139).
Lex Gabinia tabellaria: secret ballot in elections. Praetor Cornelius Hispalus expels astrologers (Chaldaei) and Jews (Valerius Maximus 1.3.3).
Consuls briefly imprisoned by tribunes over the levy. Brutus (later Callaicus) campaigns in Lusitania and Gallaecia; founds Valentia.

Mancinus' army trapped at Numantia; quaestor Tiberius Gracchus negotiates a treaty, later repudiated, and Mancinus is handed over naked to the Numantines (136), who refuse him. Lex Cassia tabellaria extends the ballot to trials (except perduellio).
Slave revolt in Sicily under Eunus begins (dated 136 or 135).
First Sicilian Slave War spreads; Eunus styles himself King Antiochus.
Aemilianus elected to a second consulship in breach of the law against iteration; given Numantia; raises volunteers and clients.

Tribunate of Tiberius Gracchus: lex Sempronia agraria, tresviri agris iudicandis adsignandis; deposition of the tribune Octavius; Gracchus killed by Scipio Nasica and senators. Numantia falls. Attalus III bequeaths Pergamum to Rome.
Special court punishes Gracchus' supporters. Rupilius ends the Sicilian slave war and issues the lex Rupilia for Sicily. Via Popillia. Aristonicus' revolt in Asia.
First two plebeian censors. Crassus, pontifex maximus, leaves Italy to fight Aristonicus; killed 130. Speech of the censor Metellus Macedonicus on compulsory marriage.
Lentulus died in office; whether a suffect was elected is uncertain. Perperna captures Aristonicus.
Death of Scipio Aemilianus (possibly murdered) after transferring the land commission's judicial powers. Aquillius organises the province of Asia (129-126).
Annius' cognomen also given as Luscus.
Ravilla the judge famous for asking 'cui bono?'.
Lex Iunia expels non-citizens from Rome. Gaius Gracchus quaestor in Sardinia.
Fulvius proposes citizenship for the allies; sent to help Massilia against the Saluvii. Revolt of Fregellae, destroyed by the praetor Lucius Opimius.
Sextius campaigns against the Saluvii; founds Aquae Sextiae (122).

First tribunate of Gaius Gracchus: lex frumentaria, lex iudiciaria (equites on the extortion juries), lex de provincia Asia (tithes auctioned at Rome), road building, colonies. Metellus conquers the Balearics (Balearicus), founds Palma and Pollentia.
Gaius Gracchus' second tribunate; colony Junonia at Carthage; citizenship bill defeated. Livius Drusus outbids him. Lex Acilia de repetundis (partly preserved on the Tabula Bembina) dated 123 or 122.

Senatus consultum ultimum: Gaius Gracchus and Fulvius Flaccus killed with some 3,000 followers. Opimius builds the temple of Concord. Fabius (Allobrogicus) and Domitius defeat the Arverni and Allobroges; the start of Gallia Transalpina. Via Domitia.
Opimius tried and acquitted. Carbo later defends him, apostatising from the Gracchans.
Gaius Marius tribune: law narrowing the voting bridges (pontes). Metellus (Delmaticus) campaigns in Dalmatia.
Citizen colony Narbo Martius founded (118). Micipsa of Numidia dies; kingdom divided between Adherbal, Hiempsal and Jugurtha. Cato (grandson of the Censor) died in Africa.
Sententia Minuciorum on the dispute between Genua and the Langenses Viturii (CIL I2 584). Scaevola the Augur, teacher of Cicero.
Senatorial commission under Lucius Opimius divides Numidia; Jugurtha gets the richer west.
Scaurus becomes princeps senatus. Sumptuary law of Scaurus.
Three Vestals tried for unchastity (114-113); Greek and Gallic couples buried alive again; temple to Venus Verticordia. Cato defeated by the Scordisci.
Cimbri and Teutones defeat Carbo at Noreia.
Jugurtha takes Cirta and massacres Italian traders; war declared. Lex agraria of 111 (Tabula Bembina) may be dated here or 111.
Nasica died in office. Bestia's peace with Jugurtha, suspected of bribery. Lex agraria privatises the Gracchan allotments (epigraphic law, 111).
Jugurtha in Rome murders Massiva; 'urbem venalem'. Aulus Postumius' army sent under the yoke at Suthul (early 109).
Metellus (Numidicus) in Africa, with Marius as legate; battle of the Muthul. Silanus defeated by the Cimbri. Mamilian commission condemns Opimius, Bestia and others.
Hortensius condemned before entering office (or during it); Scaurus suffect.
Marius, a novus homo, given the Numidian command by popular vote and enrols capite censi volunteers. Cassius killed by the Tigurini near Burdigala (Agen?), his army sent under the yoke.
Lex Servilia Caepionis restores senators to the juries (in part). Caepio seizes the 'gold of Tolosa', which vanishes. Births of Cicero (3 Jan) and Pompey (29 Sept).

Battle of Arausio (6 October): Caepio and Mallius destroyed by the Cimbri and Teutones; Livy's figure of 80,000 dead. Jugurtha betrayed to Sulla by Bocchus. Rutilius introduces arms drill by gladiatorial trainers.

Marius re-elected in absentia; army reforms traditionally attributed to 104-102 (eagle as sole standard, mules). Jugurtha executed after the triumph. Second Sicilian Slave War (104-100). Lex Domitia: priests elected by 17 tribes.
Orestes died in office. Saturninus' first tribunate: land for Marius' veterans in Africa; lex Appuleia de maiestate.
Marius destroys the Teutones and Ambrones at Aquae Sextiae. Marcus Antonius (Orator) given a command against Cilician pirates.

Marius and Catulus destroy the Cimbri at Vercellae (Campi Raudii), 30 July. Aquillius ends the Sicilian slave war (100). Lex de provinciis praetoriis (pirate law; Delphi and Cnidus copies) of 101/100.
